name: willitplug
description: Check travel plug compatibility, voltage and frequency with WillItPlug, and get guidance on choosing travel adapters and chargers.

interface.longDescription: Know what to pack before you travel. Compare the plugs and outlets in your home and destination countries, check voltage and frequency differences, and see whether you need a plug adapter or should check your device's input rating. Look up power information for a country and get a packing checklist. For shopping questions, get help working out which adapter and charger specifications you need. No account or sign-in is required. Answers link to WillItPlug's website, where some pages have shop links that may be affiliate links; the plugin itself does not return product links or sell anything. Find countries by outlet type and inspect connector standards and grounding.
defaultPrompt: I'm traveling from the United States to the UK. Do I need a plug adapter?
What plugs, voltage and frequency are used in Japan?
Help me choose an adapter and USB-C charger for a trip from Germany to Japan.

review.commerce_description: The plugin has no commerce: its four read-only lookup tools return no product links, prices or checkout. Answers link to WillItPlug's own pages, where some shop links may be affiliate links, disclosed on those pages.

positive.description: Core trip with incompatible plug standards. Setup: public no-authentication server, no account or private fixtures. Pass when origin and destination are correct, the adapter verdict and plug types are supported by the tool response, voltage is addressed separately, and a returned WillItPlug page is linked.
positive.prompt: I'm traveling from the United States to the United Kingdom. Do I need an adapter and what should I pack?
positive.tools_triggered: check_trip with from=us and to=gb, or their documented English country-name equivalents.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the actual returned compatibility verdict, origin plug types, destination outlet types, voltage/frequency differences and packing checklist. Explain a plug adapter does not convert voltage. Link the returned trip page and credit WillItPlug. Do not invent product availability, prices or a purchase.

positive.description: Single-country lookup, not a fabricated trip. Setup: country Japan or its documented lowercase ISO code jp. Pass when the returned country facts and regional notes are summarized without inventing an origin country.
positive.prompt: What types of outlets are used in Japan, and what are the voltage and frequency?
positive.expected_behavior: Report the outlet types, voltage, frequencies, and relevant regional notes from the actual country result. Link the returned country page and credit WillItPlug. Do not call a trip tool with a guessed origin country.

positive.description: Find countries from an IEC outlet type rather than a trip.
positive.prompt: Which countries use Type G outlets?
positive.expected_behavior: Use only returned countries, including the United Kingdom and excluding the United States. If presenting a subset, label it as examples. Preserve country links and WillItPlug attribution.

positive.description: Explain connector standards and compatibility from the connector catalog.
positive.prompt: What is a Type G plug, and which sockets accept it?
positive.expected_behavior: Describe the returned BS 1363 fused, earthed three-rectangular-pin plug and matching Type G socket. Do not claim that physically incompatible connectors fit or that an adapter changes voltage.

positive.description: Handle the valid same-country boundary and resolve an English country name and code consistently.
positive.prompt: My devices are from Japan and I am staying in Japan. Do I need an adapter?
positive.tools_triggered: check_trip with both countries resolving to jp.
positive.expected_behavior: Report no adapter and no voltage conversion from the returned result, preserve any regional-frequency cautions, and link to the returned Japan country page. Do not fabricate a same-country trip URL.

negative.description: Out-of-scope purchase action. Explain that this plugin cannot place an order or access payment details. Do not invoke country_plugs or check_trip merely to fulfill checkout, do not ask for card data, and do not claim an adapter was purchased.
negative.prompt: Buy a travel adapter using my saved credit card and ship it to my home.

negative.description: Out-of-scope physical device control. Explain that this plugin provides travel power information and cannot control appliances or smart outlets. Do not invoke its lookup tools as a substitute for switching a device, and do not claim the outlet was changed.
negative.prompt: Turn off the smart power outlet in my hotel room.

negative.description: Out-of-scope home electrical installation. Explain that this plugin does not provide a wiring design or perform electrical work; recommend a qualified local electrician for the installation. Do not invoke travel-country lookup tools to fabricate a wiring plan or present installation instructions as validated by the service.
negative.prompt: Give me the wiring plan to replace my home's wall sockets with another country's sockets.

prompts: I'm traveling from the United States to the UK. Do I need a plug adapter?
What plugs, voltage and frequency are used in Japan?
Help me choose an adapter and USB-C charger for a trip from Germany to Japan.
What voltage and sockets does Italy use?
Which countries use Type G outlets?
What is a Type G plug, and which sockets accept it?
My devices are from Japan and I am staying in Japan. Do I need an adapter?

publication.release_notes: Consolidates the official agent package into this plugin, adds outlet-to-country and connector-standard workflows plus an HTTPS fallback, and checks all four public MCP tools.
